newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks regain their stride, close up.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks regain their stride, close up.

text.p: Caracas stocks regained their stride, closing up on renewed foreign bids and bullish sentiment that looks set to continue into next week, traders said.

"Foreign demand came back today ... it's been years since I've seen such positive sentiment, and if the market dips it's just another reason for investors to buy," Merinvest analyst Roberto Isasi said.
The bolsa's 19-share index gained 1.11 percent to end at 9,450.56 points as 68 million shares traded, worth 9.6 billion bolivars ($19.5 million).
Traders said the bolsa's was also partly due to continued low interest rates and high liquidity. "It has helped lend the market it's tone," Profimerca broker Miguel Gonzalez said.

Despite new commercial bank reserve requirements, which the Central Bank boosted Thursday to 15 percent from 12 percent of deposits and are due to come into force Monday, Gonzalez said the bolsa looked bullish for next week.
Upping reserve requirements sucks liquidity from the market as commercial bank are forced to place a greater proportion of their deposits into non-interest bearing Central Bank accounts.

Among traded shares, 27 rose, 13 fell and five closed flat. Traders said bid interest centered on Corimon B shares, up 5.75 percent to end at 21.15 bolivars as over 20 million shares traded, and bellwether Electricidad de Caracas, up 1.37 percent to close at 815.00 bolivars.
